Messages.Author: Jeff Hildebrand
Messages.Body:
In article <Pine.SUN.3.91.95092...@ccn.cs.dal.ca>,
Kathleen Ellis <af...@ccn.cs.dal.ca> wrote:

>I've been looking forward to the expansion but I think by the time it
>gets out I won't have any respect for Wizards left to make a purchase.

Fact. Magic is far more popular than Jyhad/V:TES is or likely
ever will be. Deal with it. WoTC is in a bad situation where demand is
massively outstripping their ability to supply. (They're pretty much
unable to keep regular Magic cards and Ice Age in stock.) Because of
extremly long lead times for signing contracts and preparing things
they planned their schedule before they realized the full extent of
the crunch. Thus they're in a situation where somebody is going to have
to wait. Given the choice between pissing off the hordes of Magic fans
and pissing off the much smaller number of Jyhad fans, it's an obvious

choice. You don't have to like it, but the level of moral indignation
running around here is ridiculous.

-Jeff

Messages.Author: Thomas R Wylie
Messages.Body:
Kathleen Ellis <af...@ccn.cs.dal.ca> wrote:
>From what I've heard in the last few days they've bumped the release date
>somewhere around December, I'm sure it's because of Homelands. The only
>expansion for Jyhad and they don't deem it important enough to get it
>out. Why should they? With everything Magic is giving them $$$$$$$.

Messages.Author: Jeff Hildebrand
Messages.Body:
In article <Pine.SUN.3.91.95100...@ccn.cs.dal.ca>,
Kathleen Ellis <af...@ccn.cs.dal.ca> wrote:

>> Fact. Magic is far more popular than Jyhad/V:TES is or likely
>> ever will be.
>

>I never stated otherwise.

No, but the comment about losing respect for WoTC for pushing
back the V:TES/DS release date instead of pushing back the release
date for Homelands isn't very consistant with the viewpoint.

>WoTC has been in the card business for a few
>years now, I think they should be well aware of how complicated things
>can get and adjust accordingly.

Yup, but the business is changing rapidly. They are trying to
deal with orders that are an order of magnitude larger than what they
were dealing with last year. Furthermore Carta Mundi is now dealing
with a lot more companies printing games than they were a year ago, so
there's a lot less flexibility in printing schedules. It seems to me
that things have been and are continuing to get more complicated.
Your expectation is a lot more realistic in a stable environment, and
the CCG market is not even remotely stable.

> Release dates shouldn't be released until they are absolutely sure.

Well it seems to me that they had an initial release date when
they first started taking orders for the game (which they have to have
in order to get distributors to list the game), and then since then
they've been very quiet. I've noticed that Tom Wylie is bending over
backwards around here to avoid saying exactly when the cards will be
out. All I've seen is that they should be out by the end of the year
with DS after V:TES. Anything else here is either the original GenCon
plan or just rumor-mongering. In comparison to some other companies,
WoTC has been following a very responsible course of action on this
front.

> Then again this is MY opinion.

And you're welcome to express it. But I'm also free to express
the opinion that some people here are letting their impatience cloud
the facts, and that's what I'm doing.
